literal: Taizong, Part Two
idiomatic: Taizong, Part Two

literal: In the third month, on day renxu, he was about to travel east on tour; Sanko said agricultural work was just beginning, requested reducing the baggage train, and urged return to court — it was granted.
idiomatic: In the third month, on renxu day, as he prepared to tour eastward, Sanko argued that the spring planting was only just underway, asked that supply wagons be cut back, and pressed for an early return to court; the Emperor agreed.

literal: On day bingyin, the Jurchen came to pay tribute.
idiomatic: On bingyin day the Jurchen brought tribute.

literal: On day guiyou, he traveled east on tour.
idiomatic: On guiyou day he set out on an eastern tour.

literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the wuyin new moon, he went to the Southern Capital.
idiomatic: That summer, on the wuyin new moon of the fourth month, he went to the Southern Capital.

literal: On day jiashen, the Jurchen came to pay tribute.
idiomatic: On jiashen day the Jurchen brought tribute.

literal: On day yiyou, he visited the hot springs.
idiomatic: On yiyou day he visited the hot springs.

literal: On day jichou, he returned to the palace and attended court before the Grand Empress Dowager.
idiomatic: On jichou day he returned to the palace and paid court to the Grand Empress Dowager.

literal: On day dingyou, the Jurchen presented bows and arrows as tribute.
idiomatic: On dingyou day the Jurchen presented bows and arrows in tribute.

literal: On day jihai, Grand Xiangwen Yelü Lubugu of the southwest frontier reported a Tangut victory.
idiomatic: On jihai day Yelü Lubugu, grand xiangwen on the southwest frontier, reported a victory over the Tangut.

literal: In the fifth month, on day jiayin, Jin again sent envoys requesting elevated titles; it was granted.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiayin day, Jin again sent envoys asking that honorific titles be conferred; the court assented.

literal: In the sixth month, on the bingzi new moon, Tuyuhun and the eastern Jurchen came to pay tribute.
idiomatic: On the bingzi new moon of the sixth month, Tuyuhun and the eastern Jurchen brought tribute.

literal: On day xinmao, Southern Tang came to pay tribute.
idiomatic: On xinmao day Southern Tang sent tribute.

literal: On day guisi, an edict ordered building the Hall of Sun, Moon, and Four Seasons, with portraits of ancient emperors and kings painted on both side corridors.
idiomatic: On guisi day an edict ordered construction of the Hall of Sun, Moon, and Four Seasons, with the deeds of ancient emperors and kings painted along both side corridors.

literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on day guihai, envoys were dispatched to present horses to Jin.
idiomatic: That autumn, in the seventh month on guihai day, envoys were sent to present horses to Jin.

literal: On day dingmao, Gulidi was dispatched as envoy to Jin, and Meiligu to Southern Tang.
idiomatic: On dingmao day Gulidi was sent as envoy to Jin and Meiligu to Southern Tang.

literal: On day wuchen, Central Secretariat Vice Chancellor Yelü Shulan Dielige was dispatched as envoy to Jin, with Linhai Army Military Governor Zhao Siwen as deputy, to invest the Jin Emperor with the title Heroic Martial and Brightly Righteous Emperor.
idiomatic: On wuchen day Yelü Shulan Dielige, vice chancellor of the Central Secretariat, was dispatched to Jin with Linhai Army Military Governor Zhao Siwen as deputy to invest the Jin Emperor as the Heroic Martial and Brightly Righteous Emperor.

literal: In the eighth month, on day wuzi, the Jurchen came to pay tribute.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuzi day, the Jurchen brought tribute.

literal: On day gengzi, Tuyuhun, Wusun, and Mohe all came to pay tribute.
idiomatic: On gengzi day Tuyuhun, Wusun, and Mohe all sent tribute.

literal: In the ninth month, on day gengxu, the Heichezi Shiwei presented famed horses as tribute.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengxu day, the Heichezi Shiwei presented famed horses.

literal: Border officials reported that Jin had dispatched Acting Minister of Works Feng Dao and Left Regular Attendant of the Drafting Office Wei Xun to present the Grand Empress Dowager's elevated title, and Left Vice Director Liu Xu and Right Remonstrance Office Grandee Lu Chong to present the Emperor's elevated title; Military Commissioner Yinniyi was then dispatched to serve as reception host.
idiomatic: Frontier officials reported that Jin had sent Acting Minister of Works Feng Dao and Left Regular Attendant Wei Xun to invest the Grand Empress Dowager, and Left Vice Director Liu Xu and Right Remonstrance Grandee Lu Chong to invest the Emperor; Military Commissioner Yinniyi was then appointed to receive them.

literal: On day renzi, an edict directed that for ministers and elders, whenever great ministers were granted ranks and titles, all were to be given brocade robes, gold belts, white horses, and gold-trimmed saddles and bridles — written into statute.
idiomatic: On renzi day an edict declared that whenever ministers and elders received high rank, they were to be granted brocade robes, gold belts, white horses, and gold-trimmed saddles and bridles — and this was entered into law.

literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the jiaxu new moon, Langjun Diligu and others were dispatched to console and inquire after the Jin envoys.
idiomatic: That winter, on the jiaxu new moon of the tenth month, Langjun Diligu and others were sent to visit and comfort the Jin envoys.

literal: On day renyin, Jin sent envoys to thank him for the investiture rites.
idiomatic: On renyin day Jin sent envoys to thank him for the investiture ceremonies.

literal: That same day another envoy came presenting single-hump camels and famed horses.
idiomatic: That same day another envoy arrived with single-hump camels and famed horses.

literal: In the eleventh month, on the jiachen new moon, the Northern and Southern Chancellors and yilijins were ordered to bestow a banquet at the guesthouse on the Jin envoys Feng Dao and the rest.
idiomatic: On the jiachen new moon of the eleventh month, the Northern and Southern Chancellors and the yilijins were ordered to host a banquet at the guesthouse for Feng Dao and the other Jin envoys.

literal: On day bingwu, the Emperor took his seat in Kaihuang Hall and summoned the Jin envoys for audience.
idiomatic: On bingwu day the Emperor received audience in Kaihuang Hall and summoned the Jin envoys before him.

literal: On day renzi, the Grand Empress Dowager took her seat in Kaihuang Hall; Feng Dao and Wei Xun invested her with the elevated title Grand Empress Dowager of Broad Virtue, Utmost Benevolence, Bright Splendor, Lofty Simplicity, and Response to Heaven.
idiomatic: On renzi day the Grand Empress Dowager sat in Kaihuang Hall while Feng Dao and Wei Xun invested her as Grand Empress Dowager of Broad Virtue, Utmost Benevolence, Bright Splendor, Lofty Simplicity, and Response to Heaven.

literal: On day jiazi, the regeneration firewood-pledge rite was performed.
idiomatic: On jiazi day he performed the regeneration investiture rite.

literal: On day bingyin, the Emperor took his seat in the Hall of Promulgating Governance; Liu Xu and Lu Chong invested him with the elevated title Emperor of Sagacious Letters, Divine Martial Prowess, Aligning with Heaven's Law, Opening Fortune, Bright Virtue and Manifest Faith, Utmost Way, Broad Reverence, Bright Filial Piety, and Successor Sage.
idiomatic: On bingyin day the Emperor sat in the Hall of Promulgating Governance while Liu Xu and Lu Chong invested him as Emperor of Sagacious Letters, Divine Martial Prowess, Aligning with Heaven's Law, Opening Fortune, Bright Virtue and Manifest Faith, Utmost Way, Broad Reverence, Bright Filial Piety, and Successor Sage.

literal: A general amnesty was declared; the era name was changed to Huitong.
idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Huitong.

literal: That month Jin again dispatched Zhao Ying bearing a memorial of congratulation, presenting You, Ji, Ying, Mo, Zhuo, Tan, Shun, Gui, Ru, Xin, Wu, Yun, Ying, Shuo, Huan, and Wei — sixteen prefectures together with maps and registers.
idiomatic: That month Jin again sent Zhao Ying with a letter of congratulation, offering sixteen prefectures — You, Ji, Ying, Mo, Zhuo, Tan, Shun, Gui, Ru, Xin, Wu, Yun, Ying, Shuo, Huan, and Wei — together with their maps and registers.

literal: Thereupon an edict designated the imperial capital as Supreme Capital, its prefecture named Linhuang.
idiomatic: Thereupon an edict raised the imperial capital to Supreme Capital and named its prefecture Linhuang.

literal: Youzhou was raised to Southern Capital; the Southern Capital was raised to Eastern Capital.
idiomatic: Youzhou was promoted to Southern Capital, and the former Southern Capital became Eastern Capital.

literal: Xin Prefecture was renamed Fengsheng Prefecture; Wu Prefecture was renamed Guihua Prefecture.
idiomatic: Xin Prefecture was renamed Fengsheng, and Wu Prefecture was renamed Guihua.

literal: The Northern and Southern Courts and the Yishi yilijin were raised to princes; chief clerks became magistrates, magistrates became prefects, prefects became military governors; tribal chiefs became Ministers of Work, darqan became deputy commissioners, madu became county magistrates, and county darqan became cavalry and infantry commanders.
idiomatic: The Northern and Southern Courts and the Yishi yilijin were ennobled as princes; chief clerks were made magistrates, magistrates prefects, prefects military governors; tribal chiefs became Ministers of Work, darqan deputy commissioners, madu county magistrates, and county darqan cavalry and infantry commanders.

literal: Posts were established for Xuanhui, Gatekeepers, Crane Control, Guest Reception, Censor-in-Chief, Vice Censor, Attending Censor, Adjudicator, Literary Shift Attendants, palace bureaus' hereditary candles, horse herds and Imperial Carriage hereditary candles; Northern and Southern Court and imperial uncle account Langjun posts became chamberlains; every department's chancellor and military governor accounts became Ministers of Work; Ershiwei Talin became Pushe; Eagle Yard, Foundry Supervision, and similar bureau chiefs became xiangwen.
idiomatic: Offices were set up for Xuanhui, Gatekeepers, Crane Control, Guest Reception, Censor-in-Chief, Vice Censor, Attending Censor, Adjudicator, Literary Shift Attendants, palace bureaus' hereditary candles, horse herds and Imperial Carriage hereditary candles; Langjun posts in the Northern and Southern Courts and the imperial uncle's household became chamberlains; chancellor and military governor households in every department became Ministers of Work; Ershiwei Talin was made Pushe; and chiefs of the Eagle Yard, Foundry Supervision, and like bureaus became xiangwen.

literal: In the twelfth month, on day wuxu, Tongkuo, Abo, and others were dispatched as envoys to Jin; by decree Feng Dao of Jin was made Acting Grand Tutor, Liu Xu Acting Grand Preceptor, and other offices each differing in rank.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuxu day, Tongkuo, Abo, and others were sent as envoys to Jin; by decree Feng Dao of Jin was appointed Acting Grand Tutor, Liu Xu Acting Grand Preceptor, and the remaining offices were adjusted each according to rank.

literal: In the second year, in the first month of spring, on day yisi, because he had received Jin's investiture, envoys were dispatched to notify Southern Tang and Goryeo.
idiomatic: In the second year, on yisi day in the first month of spring, envoys were sent to notify Southern Tang and Goryeo of his acceptance of Jin's investiture.

literal: On day dingwei, he took his seat in Kaihuang Hall, feasted the Jin envoys Feng Dao and below, and bestowed gifts differing in grade.
idiomatic: On dingwei day he held court in Kaihuang Hall, feasted Feng Dao and the other Jin envoys, and bestowed gifts of varying grade.

literal: On day wushen, Jin dispatched Gold Crow Guard General Ma Congbin and Director of Personnel Liu Zhixin with precious gifts; they were ordered distributed among the ministers.
idiomatic: On wushen day Jin sent Gold Crow Guard General Ma Congbin and Director of Personnel Liu Zhixin with precious tribute; the Emperor ordered the gifts divided among his ministers.

literal: On day bingchen, Jin sent envoys thanking him for exempting the four frontier prefectures from coin tribute.
idiomatic: On bingchen day Jin sent envoys to thank him for remitting coin tribute from the four frontier prefectures.

literal: In the second month, on day wuyin, he feasted the princes and military governors who had come to congratulate on receiving the investiture, and ordered the Crown Prince and tixin Dilian to see them off with a parting feast.
idiomatic: In the second month, on wuyin day, he feasted the princes and military governors who had come to congratulate him on the investiture, and ordered the Crown Prince and tixin Dilian to give them a farewell banquet.

literal: On day guisi, he visited the Taizu temple, bestowed goods on officials and people in the capital, and granted rewards to inner and outer ministers differing in grade.
idiomatic: On guisi day he visited the Taizu temple, distributed goods to officials and commoners in the capital, and granted rewards of varying grade to ministers within and without the court.

literal: On day dingyou, Wang Ji, concurrently Palace Attendant and General-in-Chief of the Left Gold Crow Guard, was made Acting Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: On dingyou day Wang Ji, who also served as Palace Attendant and General-in-Chief of the Left Gold Crow Guard, was appointed Acting Grand Commandant.

literal: In the third month, he hunted at the border of Niaotan Marsh.
idiomatic: In the third month he hunted along the shore of Niaotan Marsh.

literal: On day wushen, the Jurchen came to pay tribute.
idiomatic: On wushen day the Jurchen brought tribute.

literal: On day dingsi, Prince Shulü was enfeoffed as Prince of Shou'an, and Yansage as Prince of Taiping.
idiomatic: On dingsi day Prince Shulü was enfeoffed as Prince of Shou'an and Yansage as Prince of Taiping.

literal: On day jisi, a great distribution of gifts was made to the common people.
idiomatic: On jisi day the common people received a great distribution of gifts.

literal: In the fourth month of summer, on day yihai, he visited Mount Muye.
idiomatic: That summer, in the fourth month on yihai day, he visited Mount Muye.

literal: On day guisi, the Eastern Capital Circuit reported wolves eating people.
idiomatic: On guisi day the Eastern Capital Circuit reported that wolves had killed people.

literal: In the fifth month, on day yisi, selling female sheep outside the Southern Capital was forbidden.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yisi day, the sale of ewes beyond the Southern Capital was forbidden.

literal: Sinuguduo Li and others, guilty of stealing government goods, had their households registered for confiscation.
idiomatic: Sinuguduo Li and others, convicted of stealing government property, had their households registered and their goods seized.

literal: Southern Tang dispatched envoys to pay tribute.
idiomatic: Southern Tang sent envoys with tribute.

literal: On day dingwei, the tribute goods were bestowed on the ministers.
idiomatic: On dingwei day the tribute goods were distributed among the ministers.

literal: On day wushen, Uyghur Chanyu envoys requested offices; by edict they were granted in succession the ranks of prefect and county magistrate.
idiomatic: On wushen day envoys of the Uyghur Chanyu asked for offices; by edict they were promoted in turn to prefect and county magistrate.

literal: In the sixth month, on day dingchou, rain and snow fell.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingchou day, rain and snow fell.

literal: That summer the court encamped at Pinbi Marsh.
idiomatic: That summer the court encamped at Pinbi Marsh.

literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on day wushen, Jin sent envoys presenting rhinoceros horn belts.
idiomatic: That autumn, in the seventh month on wushen day, Jin sent envoys with rhinoceros-horn belts.

literal: On day gengxu, Tuyuhun came to pay tribute.
idiomatic: On gengxu day Tuyuhun brought tribute.

literal: On day yimao, Chamberlain Abo, guilty of neglect in carrying out his mission, was ordered flogged.
idiomatic: On yimao day Chamberlain Abo, convicted of failing in his embassy, was ordered flogged.

literal: In the intercalary month, on day guiwei, the Prince of Yishi, guilty of uneven tax levies, was beaten on the back with a wooden sword and released;
idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on guiwei day, the Prince of Yishi, convicted of uneven tax levies, was beaten on the back with a wooden sword and released;

literal: Also abolished the Northern and Southern Courts' people's upward deliveries, and taxes and corvée imposed on chancellors and military governors outside the old system.
idiomatic: At the same time the court abolished the tribute levied on the people of the Northern and Southern Courts and the taxes and corvée imposed on chancellors and military governors beyond what the old system allowed.

literal: On day yiyou, Dilie was dispatched to present fine Wugu horses to Jin.
idiomatic: On yiyou day Dilie was sent to present fine Wugu horses to Jin.

literal: On day jichou, because two prefects of the Southern Prince's household were corrupt, each was flogged one hundred strokes, still tied to the guard account and made ready to shoot demon-arrows; ministers beloved by the people were chosen to replace them.
idiomatic: On jichou day two prefects of the Southern Prince's household, found corrupt, were each flogged one hundred strokes, bound to the guard account, and assigned to shoot demon-arrows; ministers favored by the people were chosen to take their places.

literal: In the eighth month, on day yichou, Jin sent envoys with annual tribute, reporting submission of gold and silk for the xu and hai years at Yanjing.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yichou day, Jin sent envoys with the annual tribute, reporting payment of gold and silk for the xu and hai years at Yanjing.

literal: In the ninth month, on day jiaxu, Zubu Alidi came to pay tribute.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiaxu day, Zubu Alidi brought tribute.

literal: On day jimao, envoys were dispatched to Jin.
idiomatic: On jimao day envoys were sent to Jin.

literal: In the tenth month of winter, on day dingwei, because the Wugu tribe's pastures were rich and waters lush, an edict ordered the Northern and Southern Courts to move three shilie households to dwell there.
idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month on dingwei day, because the Wugu pastures were rich and the waters abundant, an edict ordered the Northern and Southern Courts to resettle three shilie households there.

literal: In the eleventh month, on day dinghai, the Iron Li and Dunhuang both dispatched envoys to pay tribute.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dinghai day, the Iron Li and Dunhuang both sent tribute envoys.

literal: In the twelfth month, on day gengzi, he went fishing on the Tu River.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengzi day, he fished on the Tu River.

literal: On day jiazi, among Uyghur envoys' attendants some struck one another with blades; an edict handed them to their envoy for punishment.
idiomatic: On jiazi day some attendants among the Uyghur envoys drew blades on one another; an edict left their punishment to their own envoy.

literal: In the third year, in the first month of spring, on day wuzi, the King of Wuyue dispatched envoys to pay tribute.
idiomatic: In the third year, on wuzi day in the first month of spring, the King of Wuyue sent tribute envoys.

literal: On day gengyin, the Renhuang King's consort came to court.
idiomatic: On gengyin day the Renhuang King's consort came to court.

literal: Uyghur envoys asked to observe the various states' envoys' audience ceremony; it was granted.
idiomatic: Uyghur envoys asked to witness the audience ceremony for foreign envoys; the request was granted.

literal: On day renchen, Attendant-of-Audience Abo was dispatched to Jin for the birthday rite.
idiomatic: On renchen day Attendant-of-Audience Abo was sent to Jin for the birthday ceremony.

literal: Jin presented the Tuyuhun of Bing, Zhen, Xin, and Dai who had come to submit.
idiomatic: Jin presented the Tuyuhun of Bing, Zhen, Xin, and Dai who had submitted to them.

literal: In the second month, on day jihai, Xi King Raoguning led six military governors in court tribute.
idiomatic: In the second month, on jihai day, Xi King Raoguning led six military governors to court with tribute.

literal: On day gengzi, Wugu sent envoys presenting captives from the Fulugu state; their yilijin was granted banners and drums to honor his achievement.
idiomatic: On gengzi day Wugu sent envoys with captives taken in Fulugu; their yilijin was granted banners and drums in recognition of the feat.

literal: On day renyin, the Jurchen came to pay tribute.
idiomatic: On renyin day the Jurchen brought tribute.

literal: On day xinhai, Molihumoli, envoy to the Uyghur Aslan, returned; facing robes were bestowed to reward him.
idiomatic: On xinhai day Molihumoli, envoy to the Uyghur Aslan, returned; he was rewarded with facing robes.

literal: On day yimao, the Yalu River Jurchen dispatched envoys to attend court.
idiomatic: On yimao day the Yalu River Jurchen sent envoys to attend court.

literal: In the third month, on day wuchen, envoys were dispatched to Jin reporting the tour to the Southern Capital.
idiomatic: In the third month, on wuchen day, envoys were sent to Jin to announce his tour to the Southern Capital.

literal: On day jisi, he went to the Southern Capital.
idiomatic: On jisi day he went to the Southern Capital.

literal: On day xinwei, tixin Yelü Nieligude was ordered to lead ten thousand horsemen as vanguard.
idiomatic: On xinwei day tixin Yelü Nieligude was ordered to lead ten thousand horsemen as vanguard.

literal: On day renshen, he halted at Shiling; because Xi King Raoguning and Military Commissioner Yinniyi had not come promptly to audience, they were sharply rebuked.
idiomatic: On renshen day he halted at Shiling; Xi King Raoguning and Military Commissioner Yinniyi, having failed to come promptly to audience, were sharply rebuked.

literal: On day bingzi, Lubugu reported the count of Tangut captives taken.
idiomatic: On bingzi day Lubugu reported the number of Tangut captives taken.

literal: On day guiwei, he hunted at Shuimen and captured a white deer.
idiomatic: On guiwei day he hunted at Shuimen and took a white deer.

literal: On day gengyin, an edict directed that retainers who harassed the people were to be punished under military law.
idiomatic: On gengyin day an edict declared that retainers who harassed the people would be punished under military law.

literal: On day jiawu, he visited Ji Prefecture.
idiomatic: On jiawu day he visited Ji Prefecture.

literal: On day yiwei, Jin and Southern Tang each dispatched envoys to attend court.
idiomatic: On yiwei day Jin and Southern Tang each sent envoys to attend court.

literal: In the fourth month of summer, on day gengzi, he reached Yan, readied the full imperial retinue, entered through Gongchen Gate, took his seat in Yuanhe Hall, and performed the entering-the-palace-gate rite.
idiomatic: That summer, in the fourth month on gengzi day, he reached Yan, marshaled the full imperial procession, entered through Gongchen Gate, took his seat in Yuanhe Hall, and performed the entering-the-palace-gate rite.

literal: On day renyin, envoys were dispatched to Jin.
idiomatic: On renyin day envoys were sent to Jin.

literal: On day yisi, he visited the detached villa of Garrison Commander Zhao Yanshou.
idiomatic: On yisi day he visited the country villa of Garrison Commander Zhao Yanshou.

literal: On day bingwu, Jin dispatched Xuanhui Commissioners Yang Duan, Wang Tiao, and others to inquire after his health.
idiomatic: On bingwu day Jin sent Xuanhui Commissioners Yang Duan, Wang Tiao, and others to inquire after his health.

literal: On day renzi, he took his seat in the informal hall and feasted the Jin envoys and envoys of the various states.
idiomatic: On renzi day he held court in the informal hall and feasted the Jin envoys and envoys from the tributary states.

literal: On day bingchen, Jin sent envoys presenting tea and medicines.
idiomatic: On bingchen day Jin sent envoys with tea and medicines.

literal: On day renxu, he took his seat in Zhaoging Hall and feasted the Southern Capital ministers.
idiomatic: On renxu day he sat in Zhaoging Hall and feasted the ministers of the Southern Capital.

literal: On day guihai, Jin sent envoys congratulating on the Dragon Boat Festival; the festival goods presented were bestowed on the ministers.
idiomatic: On guihai day Jin sent envoys to congratulate him on the Dragon Boat Festival, and the festival gifts they brought were distributed among the ministers.

literal: On day yichou, Southern Tang presented a white tortoise.
idiomatic: On yichou day Southern Tang presented a white tortoise.
